# Native dm-thin consistency fixture

Generated on 2026-11-27 using LVM2 2.03.31, Linux device-mapper, and the installed
thin-provisioning-tools. Reproduce with `scripts/fixtures/generate-thin-native.sh`.
Generation uses a workspace-owned directory and a private LVM configuration.

`pv.raw.gz` expands to a 96 MiB PV with a 48 MiB thin data LV, 4 MiB metadata LV,
and 16 MiB thin volume. The native thin volume contains the shared MD
`oracle.bin` at byte 0 and byte 8,392,704; unallocated blocks read as zero.
The complete 16 MiB kernel read has SHA-256:

`102d72659401e467c573ae25c7bc268b617345e16f7b9d23e5fb513f707d82a8`

`metadata.raw.gz` expands to the 4 MiB committed metadata device. `thin_check`
verified both space maps and mapping/detail trees. `metadata.xml`, `pvs.json`,
`vgs.json`, and `lvs.json` retain native observations. The pool transaction is 1,
device 1 has transaction 0, and nine mapped blocks use 64 KiB data blocks.

`pv-transaction-conflict.raw.gz` is generated by `thin_restore --transaction-id 2`.
Its restored metadata passes native `thin_check`; the containing LVM pool still
expects transaction 1. It tests a valid-format consistency conflict across layers.

The compressed images and native tool output are generated test data under MIT.
External tools are used for fixture generation only.

`tree.raw.gz` expands to a 4 MiB metadata device generated by
`scripts/fixtures/generate-thin-tree.sh`. `thin_restore` produces multi-level
mapping trees for three devices with 1024 sparse mappings each. `thin_check`
verifies both space maps and all trees. The transaction is 5, time is 7,
data capacity is 4096 blocks, and device `id` maps logical block `2 * index`
to physical block `index + (id - 1) * 1024` with mapping time 5.

`shared.raw.gz` is generated by `scripts/fixtures/generate-thin-shared.sh`.
Four devices each map 512 logical blocks to the same physical range 0..511.
Native `thin_restore` creates the space maps including overflow reference
counts, and `thin_check` independently verifies them. The transaction is 5,
time is 7, and the data device capacity is 4096 blocks.

`held.raw.gz` is generated by `scripts/fixtures/generate-thin-held.sh` using
Linux device-mapper. It includes a held metadata snapshot sharing mapping and
device-tree nodes with the active superblock. Native `thin_check` verifies
metadata reference counts. Device 1 has four mappings in the held snapshot
and eight in the active view after a subsequent write at logical byte 1 MiB.
